v.why: With edge 4 absent, removing edge 5 leaves the output node with at most one input or disconnects it, so accuracy drops much more (exps 3, 4, 6).
With edge 3 absent, edge 5 carries a larger share of the signal into node 3, so deleting it hurts more (exps 2, 4, 8, 9).
Adding a residual shortcut where there was none gives much larger gains than swapping out an existing op (exps 14, 18, 20, 21, 24 vs 13, 15, 16).
Skip-dominated cells are nearly parameter-free and weak, so adding a 3x3 conv on the final edge gives very large gains (exps 32, 33).
Filling a missing input-to-output edge adds capacity and a path, while replacing skip, avg_pool or 1x1 on that edge tends to hurt (exps 77, 81 vs 78-80).
Adding a conv to a missing edge into the output helps more than replacing an existing skip or avg_pool there (exps 93, 99 vs 96, 97).
With edge 1 absent, removing edge 0 cuts off nodes 1 and 2 from the input, collapsing the cell (exp 54).
Adding even a parameter-free path to a missing output edge helps, whereas replacing a conv with pooling loses capacity (exps 58, 64 vs 57, 59, 60).
When edge 5 is absent, node 2 does not feed the output, so adding conv capacity on edge 1 only adds wasted computation and gives consistently negative IN16 changes (exps 38, 40, 42, 46).
Without the direct input-to-output edge, every path to the output depends on node 1 or node 2, so removing edge 0 is more damaging (exps 54, 55).

raw:
The strongest pattern is structural. Node 3 (the output) is fed only by edges 3, 4 and 5. If two of those are `none`, the cell becomes fragile:
- **Removing the last live input** disconnects the output and costs roughly 25–78 points (experiments 4, 9, 54).
- **Restoring one of those inputs** recovers just as much (experiments 29, 64, 81, 99).

There are also two other patterns:
- **Replacing `none` versus replacing a real op:** adding an op where there was `none` usually helps more than swapping out an existing op (experiments 14, 18, 20, 58, 77, 93).
- **Cells made only of `skip_connect`:** these are very weak, so adding a convolution helps them a lot (experiments 32, 33, 84).

| # | Edit | Condition | Direction | Evidence |
|---|------|-----------|-----------|----------|
| 1 | edge 5 → none | edge 4 = none | lower | Exps 3, 4, 6 are worse than the parents with edge 4 live |
| 2 | edge 5 → none | edge 3 = none | lower | Exps 2, 4, 8, 9; exps 4 and 9 lose 53–74 points on C10/C100 |
| 3 | edge 3 → skip_connect | edge 3 = none | higher | Exps 14, 18, 20, 21, 24 gain far more than exps 13, 15, 16; exp 23 (all-avg_pool cell) is an exception |
| 4 | edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 0 = skip_connect | higher | Exps 32, 33 gain 20–52 points |
| 5 | edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 3 = none | higher | Exps 77, 81 gain; exps 78, 79, 80 lose |
| 6 | edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 4 = none | higher | Exps 93, 99 gain; exps 96, 97 hurt IN16 |
| 7 | edge 0 → none | edge 1 = none | lower | Exp 54 is catastrophic |
| 8 | edge 4 → avg_pool_3x3 | edge 4 = none | higher | Exps 58, 64 compared with exps 57, 59, 60 |
| 9 | edge 1 → nor_conv_3x3 | edge 5 = none | lower | Exps 38, 40, 42, 46 are negative on IN16 in every case |
| 10 | edge 0 → none | edge 3 = none | lower | Exps 54, 55 |
